html:
Nguyễn Du was a Vietnamese poet and scholar official, author of The Tale of Kiều, the best loved work of Vietnamese literature.

He was born into a powerful family of officials under the Lê dynasty. His youth was spent in the turmoil of the Tây Sơn wars, which overthrew the Lê, and he lived for years in hiding and poverty in the countryside. In 1802 Gia Long united the country and founded the Nguyễn dynasty. Nguyễn Du served the new court, though reluctantly, rising to high office, and in 1813 he went as envoy to Qing China.

He wrote poems in classical Chinese, but his fame rests on works in chữ Nôm, the script for writing Vietnamese. In The Tale of Kiều he retold a Chinese novel in 3,254 lines of Vietnamese verse. Its themes of fate, suffering and loyalty were read as a mirror of his own divided life and his country's troubles. He died in 1820, just before he was to lead a second mission to China.
